assessments.technical_explanation: The pre-release desktop build job is invoked with blanket secret inheritance. Triggers are tag pushes and manual dispatch, both requiring repository write access, and the called workflow is same-repository. Forwarding every repository secret where only the token and signing secrets are needed is a least-privilege hygiene weakness; the supplied evidence shows no untrusted trigger or exfiltration path that would demonstrate exposure.
assessments.layman_explanation: The desktop preview build receives every stored secret instead of just the ones it uses. Only maintainers can start it and it runs the project's own code, so it's a best-practice cleanup rather than a danger.
assessments.developer_action: Pass only the specific secrets the desktop build workflow needs instead of inheriting all repository secrets.

assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged expression uses a logical-operator construct that does not behave as a true ternary in the workflow expression language: when the intended 'empty' branch evaluates, its falsy value causes the fallback branch to be selected anyway. Per the adjacent in-file comment, the intent is to leave the release notes unset on re-runs so manually typed notes are preserved, so the construct defeats that intent and can overwrite a maintainer's draft notes. This is a correctness defect in maintainer-only release automation; no untrusted input, secret, or cross-boundary effect is involved.
assessments.layman_explanation: The release workflow tries to say 'if this is a re-run, keep the notes I typed; otherwise use the default text.' Because of how the condition is written, the default text wins in both cases, so a maintainer's hand-written release notes could get replaced. It is a small bug in the release recipe, not a security issue.
assessments.developer_action: Replace the pseudo-ternary with an explicit conditional (for example, setting the release-notes input only when the release state is not a draft re-run) so draft notes are genuinely preserved.
